e: Around 30,000 bottles of wine valued at €5 million are stolen in a heist at a storage facility owned by Antinori in Tuscany.
A court in Rome sentences three Egyptian security officials to ten years imprisonment for abducting Giulio Regeni.
Prime Minister Meloni announces that the country would limit the number of foreign pupils per class and prohibit burqas and niqabs in schools.
Italy announces that it will deploy warships to protect shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb.
Four Renaissance paintings attributed to Antonello da Messina are stolen in an overnight heist at the Regional Museum of Messina.
Spain suspends Schengen Area agreements with Italy for one month in response to similar measures imposed by the latter country over the 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident.
Rafael Advanced Defense Systems' contract to run an anti-drone shield is cancelled by Rome Fiumicino Airport.
A magnitude 4.7 earthquake hits Campania, injuring 26 people.
Italy suspends Schengen Area agreements with Spain, citing the 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident.
Former Autostrade per l'Italia head Giovanni Castellucci is sentenced to 12 years' imprisonment for the Ponte Morandi collapse in 2018.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni rejects claims by United States President Donald Trump that she had "begged" him for a photograph during the 52nd G7 summit in France. The remarks cause a diplomatic row, with Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani cancelling a planned visit to the United States.
Four migrant workers from Afghanistan and Pakistan are found killed inside a burnt-out minivan in Calabria.
Eight people are injured in a car-ramming and stabbing in Modena.
Italy's Sal Da Vinci finishes fifth at Eurovision 2026 in Austria with the single "Per sempre sì".
Italy denies the United States Air Force the use the Sigonella base in Sicily for operations related to the war in Iran.
Italy fails to qualify to the FIFA World Cup for a third consecutive time after losing to Bosnia and Herzegovina 4-1 on penalties at the 2026 FIFA World Cup qualification in Zenica.
Three paintings by Auguste Renoir, Paul Cézanne and Henri Matisse are stolen in an overnight heist at the Magnani-Rocca Foundation near Parma. The paintings are recovered by police in August.
Two people are killed in an avalanche at the Hohe Ferse near Ratschings.
An Italian MQ-9 Reaper is destroyed in an Iranian drone strike on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.
The Constitutional Court of Italy rules in favour of the Meloni government's 2025 decree, which significantly restricted Italian citizenship by descent.
The Italian Armed Forces base in Erbil, Iraq is struck by an Iranian missile, with no casualties or injuries reported.
The Italian Ministry of Defence states that Italy is to dispatch naval assets to Cyprus.
A magnitude 4.5 earthquake hits Sicily, damaging at least 600 homes in Ragalna.
An ambulance operator is arrested in Forlì after being accused of murdering five elderly patients between February and November 2025.
A tram derails in Milan, killing two people and injuring 40 others.
Authorities arrest Burundian national Guillaume Harushimana in Parma in connection with the 2014 murders of three Italian missionary nuns in Bujumbura.
A fire destroys the 19th century Teatro Sannazaro in Naples.
Two skiers are killed in an avalanche along the Mont Blanc massif in Courmayeur.
The 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo.
